questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I study Korean Studies, a semester as an exchange student in Korea is mandatory.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The placement test at HUFS is something the students need to be prepared for, as they dwell on teachings we had on first and second semester. I was placed on 2nd level Korean, because I hadn’t memorized passive verbs before the exam. I enjoyed the other subjects I got to choose, but language school at Hankuk is something else, and future students should be prepared to be expected to memorize a lot. From my experience, I honestly don’t know if I’d recommend Hankuk in terms of their Korean language program.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It’s a 50/50. Some things are easy to find, others are quite difficult to figure out. However it’s manageable and just takes some getting used to. We still don’t know where to see our final grades though, which is quite a downside, but this might be fixed later on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had online orientation, but is was just repetition of what was already written in a guide we had received.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found an Airbnb and we’ve been extremely happy about that! It was no problem at all, other than finding a place that lived up to all our wishes.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you can stay together with someone, it’s definitely going to be worth it! We wouldn’t have had the same experience if we hadn’t stayed together.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We didn’t check housing offers made by HUFS out, so I have no idea.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got accepted very quickly, within 24 hours we had a response that we had been accepted into HUFS. The registration process itself was also easy, though finding subjects was a bit more tricky.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Limited help from the school. I contacted them once and didn’t get a very useful response, but it must depend on who answers the emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No success whatsoever. The classes we had looked at during the registration process weren’t offered when we had to choose our subjects. We found different subjects however, and though it wasn’t easy getting those subjects, we succeeded in the end!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find plenty of subjects you’re interested in beforehand, even though you only send two of them off to be accepted by the faculty. Then you’ll be better prepared if/when some of them aren’t offered when it’s time for you to register.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They level of the courses depends on the subject, I guess.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at the Korean language program is very very different and takes a lot of getting-used-to. The other subjects are different too, but not as much, and it’s hard to properly evaluate since we had online lessons. Real time lessons would probably we quite different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Regular Korean Language Program, Organization International Law, and Understanding Culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Understanding Culture was super interesting, the teacher is an absolute sweetheart and we learned a lot. 100% recommend to consider this subject!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cost of living was the most unexpected one for us, since it’s very expensive to grocery shop unless you make Korean food, and this you can most likely eat out easier. We spend a lot more in general than we had ever thought, so I can absolutely recommend applying for any scholarships you might be able to get.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most in supermarkets - Cheese, fruit, vegetables, meat etc

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were none other than a Buddy Program, which was online

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Due to COVID it was closed down

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything you can! There’s plenty to do, plenty to see in Seoul. And definitely take weekend trips to other cities like Busan, Yeosu or to Jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not easy. It was a tough start with 14 days of quarantine, and we struggled to adjust fully. It took me about two months to adjust and feel comfortable, and it’s worth for future students to be aware that it can take a toll, but it certainly didn’t help that we had online lessons and there were a lot of restrictions when we were there the first months.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out in the evening, go to bars and talk to people! We didn’t have the option of socializing at the school, so we went out during the weekends etc instead and gained a lot of new friendships.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The heat in August, September and some of October is quite something.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness, the food, the nightlife and social life in general, Seoul by night, new experiences in plenty and they don’t have to be expensive. So many things!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you’re gonna apply for their Korean Program, be sure to memorize passive verbs and “kvotativer”, don’t be phased by their placement test and questions with no connection, and make sure to give yourself time off to enjoy the city your in and don’t get too stressed about studying.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I’ve learned a lot about studying at a Korean college, not to mention about the Korean culture in general. I’ve refined my Korean pronunciation and learned a lot about my own limits in regards to studying. Also how to simply let things happen, and not get too hung up on if you fail or not.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to how different the school system works at the Korean language program compared to our classes at KU.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
